source.title: InterPLM: Discovering Interpretable Features in Protein Language Models via Sparse Autoencoders

record.tranche_reason: The study measures feature-vector clusters and their functional specializations, bearing on the feature-family hierarchy version, but does not compare SAEs of increasing dictionary sizes.
record.gate_note: The study trains one dictionary size per ESM-2 layer, not a size sweep on matched activations. Its SAE reconstruction and steering results do not test the listed splitting or challenge versions. The cluster observations in Section 3.4 bear on V3; results cited from other work are not recorded.
record.test_reason: In a new setting (SAEs on the ESM-2-8M protein model), the study clusters SAE decoder vectors and reports geometrically close features at different levels of specificity. The authors read the TBDR cluster as a concept hierarchy, which bears on V3. It uses one dictionary size per layer (10,240), so it has no size sweep, no splitting test, and no absorption or objective comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that clustering dictionary vectors reveals groups with coherent biological roles and distinct specializations. They say the beta-barrel cluster reflects a natural hierarchy, with specialized and general detectors having similar representations.
record.recipe_differences: Uses SAEs on ESM-2 protein embeddings and clusters dictionary vectors, but trains a single selected dictionary size per layer rather than comparing increasing dictionary sizes on the same activations.
record.problems: The hierarchy evidence is based on selected feature clusters and qualitative descriptions; the study does not compare SAE sizes or report uncertainty for the cluster-specific observations.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant cluster findings were left out.

untested.parts: Whether the families arise from splitting as dictionary size grows. Whether nesting holds quantitatively across the activation sets (only max-activating examples and F1 values are reported). How common hierarchical clusters are among all clusters.
Entire version: no comparison of dictionary sizes.
Entire version: no large models or open SAE releases.
Entire version: no parent-firing gaps or absorption test, and no size or sparsity variation.
Entire version: no comparison of latents across SAE sizes.
Entire version: no comparison of objectives (e.g. Matryoshka SAEs).

missing.what: Table 10 LLM summaries: f/1503 fires on TonB-dependent transporter loops (r=.73), and f/2469 on outer-membrane beta barrels including porins and TBDRs. f/2469 is possibly the general cluster member, but the text does not state this.

record.verdict_notes: Tranche changed from T2 to T3: it is a new domain (protein LM) and the method is not aimed specifically at splitting. The evidence is three hand-selected clusters from UMAP/HDBSCAN on decoder weights of a single SAE size, with no statistics on cluster prevalence. The SAE is not an original source for V3.

versions.untested_parts: No comparison of SAE dictionary sizes or test of whether larger-dictionary features partition a smaller feature's inputs and lie near its direction.
No size-scaling test across large models or open SAE releases.
Does not test feature families across dictionary sizes or establish that they form nested splits; reports selected clusters and their functional or structural specializations.
No test of parent-latent firing gaps, absorption, or whether size or sparsity changes those effects.
No decomposition comparison between larger- and smaller-SAE latents or test for novel latents across sizes.
No comparison of SAE objectives, including Matryoshka SAEs, or test of splitting as an objective artifact.

rows.subject: ESM-2-8M-UR50D
rows.operation_detail: Clustered SAE features by dictionary vectors and examined beta-barrel cluster specializations.
rows.measure: Feature-vector cluster membership and functional specificity
rows.value: All three features were labeled as TBDR beta barrels; one was specific to TBDRs, while two also identified broader beta-barrel structures.
rows.note: The authors describe the cluster as reflecting a natural hierarchy of beta-barrel structures, with specialized and general detectors maintaining similar representations. This is a selected cluster, not a size-dependent split test.

rows.subject: ESM-2-8M-UR50D
rows.operation_detail: Measured feature–concept F1 associations for features in the TBDR beta-barrel cluster.
rows.measure: F1 association with TBDR beta barrels
rows.note: The text identifies f/1503 as the highly specific TBDR detector.

rows.subject: ESM-2-8M-UR50D
rows.operation_detail: Measured feature–concept F1 associations for the other two features in the TBDR beta-barrel cluster.
rows.measure: F1 association with TBDR beta barrels
rows.note: The text does not assign the two scores to feature IDs. It states that these features have high recall but lower precision because they also recognize other beta-barrel proteins.
rows.check: The lower F1 values (.793, .611) are the evidence for the general beta-barrel level of the hierarchy (high recall, lower precision), not a weaker effect. Mark observed as part of the TBDR hierarchy. The two scores are not tied to feature IDs.

rows.subject: ESM-2-8M-UR50D
rows.operation_detail: Clustered features by dictionary vectors and compared kinase-feature activation patterns.
rows.measure: Shared cluster membership and activation-pattern specialization
rows.value: The three features showed subtle spatial preferences: one activated on the conserved alpha helix and beta sheet preceding the catalytic loop, while others concentrated near distinct regions around the loop; all maintained activation > 0.8 on their respective maximum examples.
rows.note: The authors say the features identify similar kinase subtypes despite different peak activation positions. No nested size-dependent relationship is tested.
rows.check: The kinase cluster shows geometrically close, related features that differ in location within the binding site. The authors describe these as identifying similar kinase subtypes, so the cluster is a family of siblings and no general/specific nesting is shown. It is partial for the hierarchy part of V3, not observed.

rows.subject: ESM-2-8M-UR50D
rows.operation_detail: Examined activation patterns of features in a glycosyltransferase cluster.
rows.measure: Cross-feature activation on maximally activating examples and spatial locations
rows.value: Feature 6262 had minimal activation on the other two features' maximally activated examples; the other two activated on all examples. On a separate protein, their activated locations were nearby but focused on different regions.
rows.note: This is a selected feature cluster with asymmetric selectivity and nearby but distinct activation locations; it does not establish nesting across SAE sizes.
rows.check: The glycosyltransferase cluster shows an asymmetry: f/6262 is more selective, and the other two fire on all examples. This hints at nesting but is shown qualitatively on max-activating examples only.

relation.reason: The authors read the decoder-vector clusters as hierarchy evidence, and their own results bear on V3.

tranche.reason: New setting (SAEs on a protein LM) with a result bearing on V3 (a geometrically close family with specific and general detectors). It does not compare dictionary sizes.

source_check.notes: One SAE per layer, selected from 20 (Methods: 10,240 latents; Results line 244 says 10,420, likely a typo). Clusters come from UMAP/HDBSCAN on decoder weights. Three selected clusters; only the TBDR one has F1 numbers. Unlabelled features are in layer 4 by the paper's convention.

statements.correction: Layer 4 follows the paper's convention (line 264: f/N means layer 4 unless stated). Three TBDR-labelled features in one cluster; f/1503 F1 .998; the other two F1 .793 and .611 (high recall, lower precision, as the authors themselves say); the authors call it a natural hierarchy of beta-barrel structures.

Kinase: three close features peak on different binding-site regions; all are >0.8 on each other's max examples; the authors say they identify similar kinase subtypes. Glycosyltransferase (2244, 6262, 9047): the authors state 6262 appears more selective, with minimal activation on the other two's max examples. The other two activate on all examples, at nearby but different locations. This is a qualitative general/specific asymmetry on max-activating examples only.
statements.problem: The kinase part is right. For glycosyltransferase, the text reports a general/specific asymmetry (6262 is more selective; the other two fire on all examples), so calling both clusters sibling specializations with no general/specific level misreads that cluster. Also, the authors state that 6262 is more selective; that is not just the verdict's reading.

statements.correction: TBDR-specific f/1503 (F1 .998) sits in one cluster with two broader beta-barrel features (F1 .793, .611). One selected SAE per layer on ESM-2-8M. No co-activation rates are measured, as differences_stated notes.
One selected dictionary per layer; clusters from UMAP/HDBSCAN on decoder weights; no comparison across dictionary sizes.
Only selected clusters are shown; no rate of hierarchical clusters and no null are reported.
The ESM-2-8M clusters are within one dictionary, with no size comparison.

Kinase: similar kinase subtypes with different peak positions; each feature >0.8 on the others' max examples. Glycosyltransferase: 6262 is more selective; the other two activate on all examples at nearby but different locations. Qualitative only.
statements.problem: The kinase cluster fits 'sibling specializations without a general/specific level'. The glycosyltransferase cluster does not: the text reports that 6262 is more selective while the other two fire on all examples.

statements.correction: ESM-2-8M: a TBDR cluster with a specific detector (f/1503, F1 .998) and two broader beta-barrel features (F1 .793, .611).
